Hope philosophy quotes

Philosophy quotations on hope, gathered from verified English renderings across traditions.

7 passages · 6+ thinkers in this selection

Why this theme matters

This theme page collects 7 English passages that touch hope as a philosophical concern—whether as a concept to define, a value to pursue, or a problem to examine.

In the history of philosophy

Related discussions appear across Greek, Chinese, Indian, Islamic, and modern European traditions. Use the quotations below as entry points, then follow thinker pages for fuller context.

Thinkers in this collection

Albert Camus , Rabindranath Tagore , Gabriel Marcel , Hannah Arendt , Dante Alighieri , Liang Qichao

Frequently asked questions

What did philosophers say about hope?

They approached hope from ethics, metaphysics, politics, and lived practice. The passages below show several of those angles in compact form.

Where can I find philosophy quotes about hope?

This archive page is organized for that search intent: verified English quotations, with links to thinkers and related themes.

How should I read these quotations?

Read the sentence first, then check school and source. A quotation is a doorway into an argument, not a substitute for the surrounding text.

  1. There are more things to admire in men than to despise.
    Albert Camus
    Philosophy of the Absurd
  2. Faith is the bird that feels the light and sings when the dawn is still dark.
    Rabindranath Tagore
    Humanism
  3. Hope consists in asserting that there is at the heart of being… a mysterious principle which is in connivance with me.
    Gabriel Marcel
    Christian Existentialism
  4. Even in the darkest of times we have the right to expect some illumination.
    Hannah Arendt
    Political Philosophy
  5. In the midst of winter, I found there was, within me, an invincible summer.
    Albert Camus
    Philosophy of the absurd
  6. Abandon all hope, you who enter here.
    Dante Alighieri
    Medieval Thought
  7. If the youth are wise, the nation is wise; if the youth are prosperous, the nation is prosperous; if the youth are strong, the nation is strong.
    Liang Qichao
    Modern Chinese Enlightenment Thought
